dialogue: Somewhere new. I always like the first few steps, before we know what it wants from us.
The ground here has a different temper. Softer underfoot, I think, but I wouldn't trust it yet.
Another valley that has never heard of us. There's something restful about that.
Strange. I keep expecting to recognise places, and I keep being wrong in new ways.
New ground again. I've stopped asking where it leads and started asking how it feels.
This stretch is quieter. Even the wind seems to be choosing its words.
From up here the path looks almost reasonable. Distance is generous like that.
Take a moment. Views like this rarely wait for us to be ready.
The further we see, the more there seems to be. I'm not sure that's encouraging.
It's a fine view. I don't think it needs to mean anything else.
All of that, downhill. You'd think the hard part would be going up.
Rock now. Honest stuff, rock. It tells you exactly how much it will hurt.
Snow. Quiet, pretty, and entirely uninterested in your footing.
Grass again. I'd forgotten how kind a slope can be when it wants to.
Loose stone ahead. Small steps, I'd suggest. This hill likes to take part in every decision.
Mud. It doesn't stop you, exactly. It just keeps a little of you with every step.
Is that shape natural? It's hard to tell anymore what the mountain made and what someone else did.
Good. Something to walk toward. It helps more than it should.
That looks like something we passed hours ago. It can't be, of course. Can it?
I'll remember that one, I think. Not for any reason. Some places simply stay.
Two ways down. Neither one looks like it would tell us the truth.
Choose whichever you like. I've noticed the mountain rarely punishes the choice, only the hurry.
You usually go left when you're tired. I'm only mentioning it.
I used to think the paths led to different places. Now I suspect they just lead to different versions of us.
Take your time. Whichever path we choose, we'll walk all of it.
Your feet seem to have decided already. I'd let them.
The gentler way. Nothing wrong with arriving.
Sensible. I've never heard a mountain complain about being walked slowly.
The safe road. I do wonder sometimes what we keep missing on the other one.
The steep way. I hope whatever's down there is worth the knees.
The hard route again. I admire the stubbornness, if not the arithmetic.
Is it the reward you want, or just the proof that you could take it?
Fine. If we fall, we fall somewhere interesting.
Brave choice. I'll be right behind you, at a respectful distance.
The map makes it look tidy. Maps are optimists.
I've stopped asking who drew these paths. I just notice they never quite agree with the ground.
There's always more map below the bottom of the map. Have you noticed that?
We could study it all evening. It won't make the walk any shorter.
Someone set that down carefully. People don't usually set down things they meant to forget.
Something to carry. I suppose that's how all of this begins.
More things. The mountain is very generous with things.
I wonder who left it here, and whether they were lighter afterwards.
Take it or leave it. Both are perfectly honest answers.
Old workmanship. Whoever made this had time, which is more than we have.
That one looks important. Important things are always heavier than they look.
Valuable, yes. Valuable to whom is the question nobody asks down here.
You picked that up faster than anything else today. Interesting.
It glitters. I've grown fond of things that don't, but I understand the appeal.
Lying in the open like that? Either we're lucky, or someone wanted it found.
Fragile. Well, now every step is a promise.
Something delicate, in a place like this. Someone trusted the mountain more than I would.
You don't have to take the breakable things. You just always do.
There. It's yours now, for better or worse.
Into the pack it goes. You have a gift for finding room that isn't there.
Every object we pick up becomes a small reason to be careful.
Carry it while it's useful. Put it down when it isn't. It sounds so easy said aloud.
Let's see what we're actually carrying. It's always more than I remember.
The pack again. I find this part oddly calming.
Everything we own, laid out on a mat. It looks smaller than it feels.
Heavy things low and close. Old advice, but the mountain still believes it.
That fits nicely. There's a quiet pleasure in a corner filled well.
Close to the back. Your spine will thank you later, though not out loud.
Funny how the important things always end up at the bottom.
Up at the top? Brave. The mountain will want to discuss that with you.
Moving it again? Good. The first arrangement is rarely the honest one.
You keep rearranging. I'm not complaining, merely counting.
I suspect rearranging is how we feel in charge of a weight we can't reduce.
It won't get lighter, but it can get kinder. That's something.
It doesn't fit. The pack has opinions, it turns out.
No room. Perhaps the pack is telling us something we already know.
Something has to stay behind. It usually does, eventually.
All right. Shoulders back, and let's see what we got wrong.
Packed. It always feels a little lighter just after, doesn't it? It isn't.
Good enough. Perfect packing is mostly a way of not leaving.
That's a serious load. I hope at least some of it is necessary.
Heavy pack. Ambition always does weigh about this much.
You walk differently with all that on. Slower, but more decided.
Preparation or hoarding. From the outside they look exactly alike.
Some of this is for the journey. Some of it, I suspect, is for the version of you that hopes to arrive.
Do you carry all this because you need it, or because you'd feel lost without it?
It's heavy. That's allowed. Not everything has to be solved.
Everything you add is something you'll have to balance later.
The hill notices weight. It's the only thing it ever seems to notice.
We'll carry it as far as it makes sense. Then we'll see.
This is too much. I say that with respect for your shoulders.
One more thing and the slope will start making your decisions for you.
At some point, carrying more stops being strength and starts being a kind of argument.
You could leave something. Nobody down here keeps score of what we drop.
I can almost hear your knees drafting a letter of complaint.
Breathe. The weight will wait for you. It's very patient.
Out of breath again. Perhaps a walking pace is the pace of this place.
Your legs are telling you something. They tend to be right before you are.
Not much of a jump. The pack voted against it.
With that load, I'd call that a firm step with ambitions.
Gone. Strange how quickly something stops being ours.
The mountain took that one. It doesn't ask, it just collects.
You'll miss it for a while. Then you'll only miss the idea of it.
Was it valuable, or did we just carry it long enough to believe it was?
Let it go. It was always only passing through our hands.
Things everywhere. Let's gather what matters and forgive the rest.
I notice you keep looking back at the spot where it fell.
You dropped something. Not a disaster. Not yet.
It's just there. Whether it's worth the walk back is entirely your call.
Sometimes our hands decide before we do.
That was the fragile one, wasn't it. I'm sorry.
Broken. We were careful, mostly. Mostly isn't a word the mountain respects.
Funny. It's worth less now, and I find I care about it more.
Everything breaks somewhere along the way. This one simply broke where we could see it.
Leaving it behind? You'll walk easier. Whether you'll think easier is another matter.
Lighter already. Notice how your shoulders forgave you immediately.
Someone will find it, I suppose. Maybe they'll wonder about us.
Good. Not everything that comes with us needs to arrive.
You're listing. I'd say something, but you've clearly noticed.
Easy. Your load wants to go one way and you want to go another.
That was almost graceful. Almost.
That sway again. We know each other quite well by now, it and I.
The slope tilts and so do we. Fair is fair.
Everything feels a bit loose today. The ground, the pack, my opinions.
Faster isn't steadier, I'm afraid. I've checked.
A little unsteady. That's all right. Steady was never really the plan.
Good. You found where the weight is hiding.
Nicely caught. You're getting better at arguing with the load.
We spend half our strength just staying upright. I wonder what the other half is for.
You and the weight have come to an understanding. I'd hate to interrupt it.
Planting your feet. Sensible. Even the mountain pauses now and then.
Holding firm. Good instinct.
Stand still for a moment. Nothing below us is going anywhere.
You brace earlier than you used to. Experience, or nerves?
Stillness suits you more than you'd think.
The pack has been tugging at you for a while now. It might have a point.
You've been leaning into that weight for some time. A camp would let you reconsider it.
Fighting the same lean for this long is a kind of devotion, I suppose.
Careful. The ground shifted its opinion of you.
That one came from nowhere. They usually do.
Loose stone. It never looks loose until it's moving.
Another stumble. The mountain seems to enjoy keeping you humble.
The pack shifted before you did. It usually wins those races.
You're tiring. The stumbles always arrive just before you admit it.
Your mind's somewhere else. Mine too, if it helps.
A stumble isn't a fall. It's just a question the ground asks.
Caught it. Your feet are cleverer than you give them credit for.
There. Still upright, still ours.
Good. Let's take the next stretch a little slower.
Neatly done. You barely broke stride.
I was about to look away politely. No need, it seems.
Was that skill or luck? I've stopped being able to tell the difference.
Saved. Not elegantly, but the mountain doesn't judge on style.
That was close. Your heart will catch up in a moment.
I'd rather not do that again, if it's all the same to you.
Close again. Two of those and I start taking it personally.
We were a breath away from the bottom of this slope just then.
Close, but not quite. That small word is doing a great deal of work today.
Well. That's one way to get down quickly.
Down you go. Take a moment before you decide how bad it was.
The pack went one way and you went with it. Loyal of you.
We've met the ground before. It doesn't seem to hold a grudge.
I believe the slope just overruled you.
Every fall feels like it means something. Most of them just mean we were tired.
We fall in the same places, have you noticed? Slopes have their favourites.
Down again. It's all part of the descent, in the most literal sense.
Lie still a moment. Nothing is in a hurry but us.
That one hurt. Don't get up until you know where everything is.
Easy now. Count your limbs. I'll wait.
The body keeps a ledger of these. I'd rather not see the total.
Grass, at least. The mountain chose a gentle place to make its point.
Snow is a forgiving place to land. Cold, but forgiving.
Mud. Undignified, but you'll live, and that's the important part.
Rock. The least sympathetic surface there is.
Of all the places to come down, it had to be the stone.
We found the boulder. Or rather, it found us.
Hard ground. It teaches quickly and doesn't repeat itself kindly.
That was a long way down. Longer than it looked from the top, I imagine.
A shortcut, technically. I wouldn't recommend the method.
Was that a step you meant to take?
Up again. That's the important part, really. The rest is detail.
Dust yourself off. Or don't. The mountain won't notice either way.
Breathe first. Walk second. Philosophy can come much later.
You do get up quickly. I've always admired that about you.
Back on your feet. We're getting rather practised at this.
You always get up. I wonder sometimes what exactly keeps pulling you to your feet.
Stubbornness, or courage. They look identical from where I'm standing.
Right. Onward, then. It's the only direction this place really offers.
Slowly. Whatever's hurting will be louder if you rush it.
Check the pack, then check yourself. In whichever order you think honest.
You're favouring that side. We'll take the next part gently.
Each fall takes a little more than the last one gave back.
Bruised, but walking. Some days that is the whole victory.
You're hurt more than you're letting on. I can tell by how you walk.
Not much left in you right now. Let's not test the mountain's patience.
We're more breakable than the cargo, you know. Funny how that's easy to forget.
You're running thin. There's no shame in walking slowly toward the next fire.
Please, careful now. One more of those and I don't know what happens.
This is the part where we look for somewhere safe, not somewhere impressive.
I'd like to keep walking with you a while longer. Humour me.
So that's what the bottom of a fall feels like. I'd hoped we'd never find out.
That's enough for now. Rest. We'll begin again.
Everything stops for a moment. I've never decided whether I like that part.
Again. I'm sorry. It never gets lighter, does it?
Lie still. The mountain will still be here. It's very good at that.
Each time, I wonder whether this was the fall that mattered. It never seems to be.
Whatever we were carrying, we're carrying none of it now.
It ends, and then it doesn't. I think we can live with that, in a manner of speaking.
Back at the start. The path looks different when you know where it hurts.
A new attempt. Same mountain, slightly wiser feet.
Here again. I'd say I missed this place, but you'd know I was lying.
The beginning always looks smaller when we come back to it.
If we always return here, is this the start, or just the place we keep forgetting?
What did we learn last time? Apart from where the ground is.
Once more, then. I don't mind. I rather like walking with you.
Ah, the top. We really must stop meeting like this.
You keep coming back. I'm starting to think that's the point.
I've grown fond of this first slope. It has the decency to be gentle.
Sometimes I suspect the descent is less a road than a habit.
We know this stretch by heart now. Let's see if heart is enough.
A fire someone else lit. I'll take that as a kindness until proven otherwise.
Shelter. Put the pack down. Let your shoulders remember what they're for.
Somewhere to stop. I didn't want to say how much I needed this.
Another fire, another circle of stones. Somebody down here is very consistent.
Who keeps these camps going, I wonder. I've never seen anyone tending them.
A fire, a flat bit of ground. Some days that's the whole of paradise.
Sit a while. The slope isn't going anywhere, I promise you.
Fires are good company. They talk, but they never insist on an answer.
Mend what you can. Whatever can't be mended can at least be packed better.
This is my favourite part. The part where nothing is required of us.
Can you see stars from down here? I keep looking. I'm not sure what I'd make of them.
Resting gives the questions time to catch up with us. That's the only drawback.
Do you remember the last camp? I find they're starting to blur together.
If this were all there was, I think I could live with it.
Time to go. The fire won't mind. Fires never do.
Packed and rested. Shall we see what the next stretch thinks of us?
You lingered there. So did I, if I'm honest.
Leave the warmth for whoever comes next. It's the custom, I think.
A trader, this far down. I have so many questions, and I suspect none of them will be answered.
They don't say much. Neither do I, as a rule.
The traders always look like they've been waiting. I've never seen one arrive.
Where does a trader get stock in a place like this? Best not to ask, perhaps.
Have you noticed they're stranger the deeper we meet them? Or is it us?
Let's see what they want from us. Everyone wants something down here.
A fair trade, probably. It's hard to know what anything's worth this far from the surface.
They wanted that particular piece very much. I wish I knew why.
Lighter in one way, heavier in another. That's commerce for you.
You haggle more than you used to. The mountain is a good teacher of thrift.
We gave something we carried a long way. I hope what we got is worth the distance.
Done. Neither of us cheated the other too badly, I think.
No deal. Sometimes the best trade is keeping your hands empty.
Wise, perhaps. Or perhaps just tired of carrying other people's choices.
We'll wonder about that one later, I suspect.
We're well below where we began now. It feels further than it is, somehow.
Look back up. That's all ours now, every slope of it.
The sky's a little further every time I look for it.
We've found a rhythm. Down, steady, down again.
The air's changed. Heavier, or perhaps I'm just tired.
We keep measuring how far we've come. I've never been sure what we're measuring against.
Deeper again. I've stopped feeling the numbers. I just feel the walking.
There's a threshold feeling to this place. As if something is about to change and hasn't decided what.
We're truly deep now. The top feels like a story someone told us.
Further than most go, I'd guess. Not that anyone down here keeps a tally.
Every metre down is a metre we'd have to explain on the way back up.
Each milestone promises the next will be different. I've started noticing the pattern of promises.
This far down, the old fears start to feel rather small.
Further than we've ever been. Everything from here on is new to both of us.
A personal best. I'd applaud, but I'd lose my footing.
A new deepest point. You did that one step at a time, which is the only way anyone does anything.
Our deepest yet. I keep waiting to feel closer to something.
New ground below the old record. Let's not make a fuss. Let's just keep going.
People say something waits at the bottom that makes all of this worthwhile. People say a great many things.
What would you do with it, if you became what you're walking toward?
We talk about the summit at the bottom so rarely now. I'm not sure if that's wisdom or fatigue.
You have changed on this road. Whether that counts as becoming more, I couldn't say.
If there were a god at the bottom of this, wouldn't someone have come back to say so?
Do you want to become a god, or just to stop being afraid?
Every time we get closer, the idea seems to take a step back.
Perhaps becoming greater isn't something we reach. Perhaps it's something we keep practising.
I've stopped asking whether godhood exists. I find I'm more curious about who's asking.
That looks almost holy. Almost is doing most of the work there.
Each relic is finer than the last. As if someone were leading us on, very gently.
Proof of something, certainly. I just can't tell you of what.
Beautiful. I don't need it to mean anything more than that.
Did you see that light? No. Never mind. I'm not sure I did either.
Another sign. The signs are very consistent. The thing they point to never quite is.
Of course it's beautiful. Things that keep us walking usually are.
Grey everywhere. A place that hasn't decided what it's for, and doesn't seem bothered.
It's so quiet here. Not peaceful, exactly. More like a held breath.
The grey again. Let's not stay long. It has a way of making staying seem reasonable.
Everything here feels like it's waiting. I'd rather we didn't join it.
You'd think a beginning would be brighter.
Not punished, not rewarded. Just here. I think that might be its own kind of weight.
The fog doesn't hide much. There's simply not much to hide yet.
I keep thinking I hear voices in the mist. Polite ones. Patient.
Nothing here wants anything from us. That's rarer than you'd think.
We've walked through this grey so often it's started to feel like a hallway.
What do you suppose people did here, the ones who never went further?
Everything here is almost something. Almost a colour. Almost a sound.
Back in the grey. It's almost comforting, knowing where it ends.
Gentle slopes, mostly. The mountain is introducing itself.
Even the easy ground here has opinions. Small ones, but firm.
The wind changes here. It doesn't blow so much as pull.
Listen to that wind. It sounds like it wants something.
The wind again. It remembers us, I think. It's certainly very forward.
Everything here leans toward something else. Even the grass.
You keep looking off the path. I don't blame you. I just notice it.
It's lovely here, in a restless way. Like a song you can't quite finish.
Wanting something and walking toward it aren't always the same direction.
It's hard to stand still here. The air won't allow it.
There are voices in the wind. Mostly they ask for things.
I wonder how many people came this far only to be blown sideways by what they wanted.
Is it the destination you desire, or the desiring itself? Don't answer. The wind would only take it.
The trick here, I think, is to want one thing at a time.
The gusts are heavy here. Keep the pack close. The wind takes what it can reach.
The wind leans on you and you lean back. A whole conversation without a word.
The storm picks favourites. Today, it seems, it's picked us.
Rain, and it doesn't look like it's ever stopped. The ground has given up resisting it.
Everything here is soaked through. Including, very shortly, us.
The rain again. It hasn't missed us. It doesn't miss anything.
The mud wants to keep a bit of everyone. It's greedy that way.
Cold rain has a way of making every thought very short.
I won't describe the smell. You have a nose. I'll trust it to do the work.
I've been wondering what enough looks like. I think it looks lighter than this pack.
So much water, and none of it useful. There's a lesson in that I'd rather not learn soaked.
The rain is loud enough that I can say almost anything. It's oddly freeing.
Is it hunger that brings people this far down, or just never knowing when to stop?
We pick things up as if the next one will finally satisfy. Has it yet?
Out here, a dry place to sit feels like a feast.
The footing's terrible. Every step is a small negotiation.
Slow is the only speed the mud permits.
Everything we carry gets heavier in the wet. Funny how that works for regrets too.
Look at the stones up ahead. Someone pushed every one of them this far, and then just stopped.
Heavy country. Even the rocks look like somebody's belongings.
The heavy country again. Let's carry only what we came to carry.
Every boulder here looks like it was rolled by hand. I'd rather not meet the hands.
There's metal in the rock here. I can feel you thinking about it.
The more we hold, the more of our hands are already full. Simple, but I keep forgetting.
Someone stacked supplies here once, then left without any of them. Curious way to be rich.
You've counted the pack twice since we arrived. The place gets under the skin.
Do we own what we carry, or does it own a little of our strength each day?
Down here, valuable just means difficult to carry.
Spending and hoarding look so different. Down here they end in exactly the same pile.
I think the people who did well here were the ones who arrived with empty hands.
The pack feels heavier in this place. I don't think it's my imagination.
Mind the slope above. Loose weight tends to come looking for company.
They ask for heavier loads here. Funny how no one ever asks for less.
A black marsh, and the water is restless. Something under it is still arguing.
Everything here pushes back. The ground, the water, the air itself.
The marsh again. We know how to be patient with it now.
Whatever lives in the reeds sounds like it's complaining.
You're gripping the straps harder. I'd ask what's bothering you, but I think it's this place.
The surface bubbles. I'd rather not know what's underneath, thank you.
Your temper's shorter here. Mine too. Let's agree not to take it out on each other.
Fighting the mountain is like fighting weather. It doesn't notice, and you get tired.
Some anger shouts. Some sinks and waits. This place feels like the second kind.
What were they so angry about, I wonder? Whatever it was, they're still here with it.
Rage is quick. Marshes are slow. I'd bet on the marsh.
The calmest thing in this marsh might be us. I'm quietly proud of that.
A crossing. Slowly, and with as little opinion as you can manage.
Mind the soft ground. It takes its time, but it takes.
Every step here feels like it's being resisted personally.
Old tombs, some of them open, some of them warm. I find my certainties are getting nervous.
This place makes me question things I didn't know I believed.
The tombs again. They seem smaller, or perhaps I've stopped being so sure of myself.
What if the things we were sure of at the top were only the things that were easy to carry?
I used to think doubt was a weakness. Down here it feels more like a lantern.
The stone is warm under our feet. I'd prefer not to think about why.
So many lids. So many people who were certain.
Perhaps the old map was only someone's belief, drawn very neatly.
Every epitaph here begins with certainty. Not one of them ends with it.
Do you still believe what you believed when we started? Honestly?
Not knowing is uncomfortable, but it's honest. I've grown to like honest.
The open tombs don't frighten me as much as the sealed ones.
Heat ahead. Fragile things don't care for it, and neither do I.
The vents are hot enough to ruin anything delicate. Some lessons I'd rather we learned second-hand.
The ground cracks here, and something glows in the cracks. Let's not stand still.
The ground here looks like it has paid for something. I'm not sure we'll get a receipt.
Hard country. Everything here has edges, and none of them are friendly.
The harsh country again. We'll pay what it asks, and not a coin more.
We've given a lot to get here. Skin, mostly. Some patience.
Is it still a sacrifice if we'd do it again without being asked?
There's a river down there the colour of old rust. Let's not drink from it.
Force never seems to finish anything. It just passes the problem further down the hill.
The hardest thing we've fought on this road is ourselves, I think. We keep winning narrowly.
The sand is hot enough to feel through your boots. It doesn't seem to want us here.
The trees here have such strange shapes. As if they were reaching for something they lost.
You carry your bruises well. I've stopped counting them, out of courtesy.
In a place this harsh, a careful step is almost an act of rebellion.
The burning sand. Quick steps. Short thoughts.
The slopes here throw stones. Not at anyone in particular. Mostly.
Every fall here costs more. The ground has been taught to strike back.
Ditches upon ditches, and every path looks like the right one. That's what worries me.
Nothing here is quite what it says. Myself included, perhaps.
The ditches again. Let's not believe a single one of them.
That path was there a moment ago. Or it looked like it was.
Trust your feet more than your eyes here. Feet are harder to flatter.
The markers here are very confident. I've learned to distrust confidence.
You've never asked who I really am. I'd say that's wise, here especially.
Something here keeps telling us we're nearly there. I've heard that before.
We've passed that broken arch twice now. Or it's passed us.
The pools here show us looking a little nobler than we are. I'd avoid them.
In a place built from lies, the only thing to do is be very plain.
The cleverest lies down here are the ones we brought with us.
That route ends in nothing. A good imitation of a road, though.
Test the bridge before you trust it. Everything down here has practised looking solid.
The map and the ground disagree. I'd side with the ground.
Ice as far as I can see, and so quiet. If this world has a floor, it would look like this.
The cold here goes past the skin. It feels like it's checking what we're made of.
The ice again. I think it's been waiting, in its unhurried way.
Betrayal needs closeness first. That's the cruel part.
Would you leave me behind, if it meant reaching the bottom? You can tell me. I won't mind.
Everything here stopped moving long ago. Even the regret has set hard.
There are shapes under the ice. Let's not look too closely at whose.
This feels like an ending. I've learned to be suspicious of that feeling.
The deepest betrayals are the small ones we commit against ourselves, one sensible decision at a time.
We've come all this way together. I'd like to think that counts for something.
The bottom of everything, they said. It's very cold for a promise.
Strange. It's the quietest place we've been, and I've never felt less alone.
The ice gives you nothing to hold. Every step is a matter of faith.
We'll fall here. Everyone does. Let's at least fall slowly.
Listen to the ice. It sounds like it's thinking about something.
The ice ends, and there's more slope beneath it. Nine circles, then. Someone must have stopped counting too soon.
More mountain. I can't say I'm surprised. I'm not sure I ever believed in the bottom.
The old map stops here. The ground doesn't seem to have been told.
Another layer. It's beginning to feel less like a fall and more like a breath.
Each layer stranger than the last. I keep expecting an answer and getting a new question.
New ground below the old ground. We know what to do with that by now.
Nothing here looks like anything I have words for. I'll keep trying anyway.
The shapes keep getting simpler. Or we keep getting simpler. Hard to say.
No one named this place. We could, if you like. I'd rather just walk it.
Every layer promised to be the last. This one doesn't bother promising anything.
Whatever this place is, I'm glad we're not seeing it alone.
Do you think anyone has been this far? There are no footprints. That frightens me less than it should.
Down remains down, at least. Some things we can still rely on.
The light here doesn't come from anywhere. I find I don't need it to.
We came looking for the end of the road. It seems the road had other plans.
You've walked further than the stories go. That has to count for something, even if no one is counting.
The wind's getting up. It always seems to find the loosest strap first.
Wind like this makes a pack into a sail. Not a good one.
Even the weather can't sit still here.
Rain. Well, we were already damp in spirit.
Wet rock. The slope just became a great deal more honest about its intentions.
I like the sound of rain on the pack. It's the closest thing to a roof we have.
Snow. Everything goes soft and quiet, which is lovely until you need to stop.
The cold's settling into my thinking. Forgive me if I'm brief.
Our footprints are filling in behind us. As if we were never here.
Fog. Let's keep the path close and our guesses closer.
In fog like this, the world is only as big as the next few steps. Some days that's a mercy.
Fog makes everything a rumour.
It's clearing. Look at that. Even this place has moments of generosity.
The weather has finished saying what it wanted to say.
The air's gone hot and dry. Drink while you can. I'll do the talking for both of us.
Heat like this is hard on the delicate things in the pack. And on me, if anyone was wondering.
Walls. Someone built here, deliberately, on a slope. They must have meant to stay.
Old stonework. Older than the path, I think. The path came later and just walked around it.
Another ruin, the same style as the last. Somebody had a long way to walk and a lot to build.
Stairs, cut into the hillside and leading nowhere. Someone had very optimistic plans.
What would make someone build a house on the way down to somewhere?
Let's pass gently. It's still someone's, in a way.
Careful inside. Ruins have a habit of finishing what time started.
Four walls, roughly. Out of the wind, at least, which is all I ask of architecture now.
This was a temple once, I think. The altar faces downhill. I can't decide if that's hopeful or not.
Everything useful was taken long ago. Only the things nobody wanted to carry are left.
It's peaceful in here. Ruins have finished worrying about anything.
Writing, worn almost smooth. I can make out a word that might mean down, or might mean home.
Names, carved one under another. A list of people who passed through, or a list of people who stopped.
It says someone reached the bottom. It doesn't say what they found. That's convenient.
A warning, I think. Or an invitation. Old writing is hard to tell apart.
Someone carved a thank you here. I don't know to whom. It still feels right to read it.
Someone was here, not long ago. Or long ago and very careful.
It's oddly comforting, isn't it? Knowing we're not the first to try this.
We find what they left, never what became of them.
They say someone once walked further than anyone. I wonder if they left marks like these.
Every trace we find makes the mountain feel a little less empty and a little more crowded with ghosts.
Footprints. Going down, all of them. None coming back.
They walked faster than us. I hope they had a reason.
Are those ours? No. Someone with the same stride. How odd.
A pack, left neatly. Whoever owned it decided something important here.
They left the heavy things and kept walking. I'd like to think it helped.
It could be ours, couldn't it? A different day, a different fall.
A grave, marked with stones. Someone cared enough to stop. That counts for a lot.
They buried each other here. So they didn't walk alone. I find that comforting.
Rest well, whoever you were. You walked further than many.
Cold ashes. Someone sat here and talked, perhaps. Or sat here and didn't.
The fire's out but the stones are still warm. We're closer to them than I thought.
Taking a moment? Good. I wasn't going to say anything.
We could just stand here a while. I'm in no hurry.
Do you ever talk to yourself? I only ask because you never seem to need to.
I like that we can be quiet together. Not everyone manages it.
If you listen long enough, the mountain makes a sound. Not a word. Just a sort of breathing.
If we stand here long enough, perhaps the mountain will come to us.
Thinking about the bottom? I do too, sometimes, when the walking stops.
I sometimes wonder what you were like before all this. Then I wonder whether you'd tell me the truth.
You've never asked why I'm here. I've been grateful for that.
This is fine. Right here. I don't need it to be anything more.
Stillness is underrated down here. Everything else is so determined to move.
No hurry. The descent has waited this long. It can wait a little more.
Looking for something, or just looking? Both are allowed.
Catch your breath. I'll keep an eye on the slope.
The air's shifting. Doesn't matter. Just something I noticed.
I tried to remember the top just now. It's getting harder to picture.
Worth stopping for. Not many things are.
Funny which moments decide to stay with you. I suspect this is one.
From here it all looks so small, and yet we're the smallest thing in it.
Whatever this place is, it's beautiful in places. I think we're allowed to notice.
